text: Match night order during the final over - fries still crackling, cheese toast bubbling. Delivery beat the surge somehow.
Festival evening and the street was jammed; the cold brew arrived sealed, chilled, not a drop lost. Impressive logistics.
Came in after the match crowds spilled out. Loud, happy, and the food still came out perfect. What an evening to be in Indiranagar.
Grabbed my usual before heading home to watch the match - three minutes even with riders crowding the pickup counter.
Meera found me a seat during the match-night madness and my filter coffee tasted exactly like always. Oasis of calm.
Match dekhne ke baad chai aur fries - sasta, garam, aur table bhi mil gayi. Festival night ka best ending.
Big match, big delivery surge, yet my paneer tikka sandwich showed up on time and neatly packed. Kudos to the riders.
Match screening at office - fourteen cappuccinos and muffins arrived labelled per person, on the dot. Nobody missed a single over.
Festival lights on, the cafe glowing pink, rose latte and a cheesecake slice shared slowly while the city celebrated outside.
Match-night dinner delivered: pasta hot, shake cold, everything upright in the bag despite the crazy streets. Full marks.
Post-match cheese toast to go - ready fast even with the festival crowd swarming. Cheap, hot, perfect walk-home snack.
Stumbled into brew during a festival evening - filter coffee, warm cinnamon roll, and the whole street celebrating outside. Magic.
Everyone rushed home for the match and the cafe went blissfully quiet. Cold brew, empty corner, most productive evening this month.
Iced latte and croissant during the festival rush - bag sealed, cup cold, croissant uncrushed. Their delivery game is strong.
Dev spotted me in the takeaway queue during match chaos and waved my order through in record time. Small-town warmth in a big city.
Festival evening date - shared a plate under the fairy glow of the pink walls, mugs steaming between us. Best seat in the city.
Match ended, crowds everywhere, and the crew still found our family of four a table fast. Kids' hot chocolates came out first - thoughtful.
Ducked in during festival traffic - my drink ready in three minutes with a lid that survived the bumpy ride home. Smooth.
Match ki jeet celebrate karne aaye - filter coffee 120, fries sasti, aur jeet ki feeling priceless. Best night out.
Festival evening team order - ten cold brews, sandwiches labelled, bagged tight for the walk back. Zero errors, zero spills.
Hot chocolate ordered at half-time, still steaming when it landed. The marshmallows had not even sunk. Match-night comfort sorted.
Cricket night and the whole city buzzing - the kulhad chai here grounded me. Staff even explained the split-flap board. Lovely people.
Post-match snacks with the gang - loud room, cheap bill, great food. The energy in here tonight was unbeatable.
Match-night feast delivered together: pasta hot, fries crisp, sauces packed separately. They clearly planned for the surge.
Festival evening, soft music inside while fireworks popped outside, dessert between us. Quiet luxury in a loud city.
Match night bhi unhone corners nahi kaate - flat white perfectly textured, aur Kabir ne extra shot bhi yaad rakha.
Ordered a waffle and hot chocolates home when the restaurant crowds got too much - arrived intact, warm, exactly as ordered.
Everyone was at the match screening so I had the cafe nearly to myself. Iced latte, empty plugs, finished the whole report.
Duck in, quick coffee, duck out - ninety seconds even with festival foot traffic outside. This counter is a machine.
Fries for the second innings - crisp, salted right, box vented so no sogginess. Whoever designs their packaging understands delivery.
Match jeet gaye, cafe mein celebrate kiya, bill itna sasta ki do baar check kiya. Perfect festival night spot.
Festival-night cinnamon roll arrived warm, icing glazed just right. The little pink stamp on the bag made my evening.
They lit the whole place up for the festival - rose latte in hand, watching the street celebrations through the window. Beautiful.
Post-match family dinner - kids' shake, our pasta, and the staff coped with the madhouse crowd like total pros. Wonderful evening.
Usual order to go before the match - six minutes amid festival chaos, still hot. The counter was moving well despite everything.
Match-night sandwich arrived warm and well wrapped. The rider took a detour around road closures so it ran a few minutes late. Fair.
Match ke baad fries aur chai - saste aur garma garam. Bas bheed itni thi ki table share karni padi.
Quiet during the match itself - cold brew, free plugs, got work done. Cheers from the street leaked in sometimes; oddly nice.
Post-match waffle with the kids - great as usual. A bit of a squeeze finding seats for four, but the staff helped us out.
Festival-order croissant and cold brew arrived intact, bag upright. Croissant a touch less flaky than fresh from the counter, but solid.
Match night ki energy cafe mein - mera cup hamesha jaisa on point. Thoda loud tha mere taste se but vibe infectious thi.
Match screening order for the team - all twelve drinks arrived, labels right, twenty minutes late in the surge. Acceptable overall.
Festival lights, a full room, cheesecake shared over slow conversation. Music a touch loud, but the celebration mood won.
Match ke baad snack leke nikle - queue lambi thi par chalti rahi. Fresh bana aur price bhi fair tha.
Half-time hot chocolate arrived still warm, marshmallows mostly intact, cup sealed. Ten minutes late in the match surge - fine.
Festival crowd everywhere and this pink cafe fit right in. My drink came chilled and floral, staff friendly even mid-chaos.
Kids' match-night dinner delivered - fries mostly crisp, pasta warm. A bit jumbled in the bag but everything arrived.
Match telecast se pehle quick drink liya. Che minute ka wait surge mein - reasonable hai, aur taste bilkul on point tha.
Festival evening glow in the cafe, my drink whisked to order. Waited a bit for a cleared table but honestly nobody minded.
Match dekh ke aaye, filter coffee aur cheese toast - dono solid. Thoda crowded tha, but rate dekh ke complain nahi.
Chilli cheese toast arrived hot during the festival rush - one corner slightly squashed in the bag, taste completely unaffected.
Pre-match pickup of drinks for the office screening. All correct, though the bag strained a bit on the walk back.
Festival dinner out - team ne crowd achhe se handle kiya aur bacchon ka khana jaldi nikala. Room loud tha but festive.
Iced drink grabbed inside during festival traffic - quick service, lid secure. It had melted a bit by the time I reached home.
Match-day fries delivery - mostly crisp, peri-peri still kicking. Ten minutes late in the surge, entirely understandable.
Festival stroll with a croissant in a stamped kraft bag - neat packaging, fresh pastry, perfect walking snack through the lights.
Flat white ab bhi great hai, though festival nights pe pricing thodi upar chadhti lagti hai. Keeping an eye on that.
Match-night crowd everywhere, energy high, saste eats aur loud laughs. Table ek baar gayi par doosri mil gayi.
Rose latte ordered mid-match - arrived warm, syrup settled at the bottom but a quick swirl fixed it. Cup sealed properly.
Everyone vanished to watch the match and I got the pink corner to myself. Quiet, productive, and my refill came fast.
Match-night crowd and four tired kids - the staff squeezed us in kindly. Longish wait for food but we were warned upfront.
Festival-date waffle and rose latte - warm, sweet, pink. Match cheers from next door bled in a little. Atmospheric anyway.
Ten cappuccinos for the match screening, all labelled, one lid ajar causing a minor leak. Otherwise smooth under surge pressure.
Cheese toast khaya counter ke saamne khade hokar - match crowd mein bhi staff theek thi. Thoda slow but paisa vasool.
Reliable even with the festival crowd squeezing in. The counter was hectic but the pour stayed proper.
Hot chocolate on match night - arrived warm in a sealed cup, marshmallows intact. Slightly dented box, no real harm done.
Match-night order - fries arrived lukewarm after an hour. The peri-peri flavour still landed, but the peak surge took its toll.
Match ke baad bheed itni ki table nahi mili, khana sasta toh tha par khade khade khana pada. Meh evening.
Post-match dinner with kids - forty minutes for pasta, noisy room, tired children. The food was fine, the timing was not.
Festival-evening delivery - croissant arrived squashed against the box wall, the drink cup tilted and leaking. Edible but a sorry sight.
Match-eve rush - the counter prioritised delivery slips and my drink took fifteen minutes, v frustrating. Good shot; broken order of operations.
Match night pe floor overwhelmed tha - mera cup great tha, par table bees minute tak clear nahi hui. Team stretched thin.
Waffle ordered at the toss, arrived around the second-innings break - cool-ish, box damp. Still tasty underneath. Time it better.
Festival evening charm, but service buckled - my chai never arrived and the filter coffee took an age. Staff were visibly swamped.
Match-night office order: all items arrived but two sandwiches were the wrong ones, and everything had cooled in transit.
Jeet celebrate karne aaye the - fries mast the, but bees minute khade rahe aur koi table nahi mili. Bitter-sweet night.
Match night brought the crowd back loud - cold brew fine, but concentrating became impossible after seven. Packed up early.
Festival date - cheesecake lovely, but the room was packed shoulder to shoulder and our table leaned. Not the relaxed night we hoped.
Match-time hot chocolate arrived barely warm, lid popped, ring of cocoa around the cup base. Could be better, honestly.
Ordered a cappuccino before the match - got a latte after a long wait at the crowded counter. Drinkable, but not what I asked for.
Kids' match-night order: shake separated and warm, fries missing their peri-peri dust. Edible, forgettable, mid.
Festival crowd ki wajah se two-seater strangers ke saath share karni padi - chai hamesha jaisi good, par experience cramped tha.
Pasta arrived after the match surge cooled it down - sauce fine, pasta lukewarm and clumping together. Reheat territory.
Flatwhite pickup on match night took triple the usual time. Riders crowding the counter choked the whole pickup flow.
Festival atmosphere was lovely but my rose milk took twenty minutes and the first table offered was still dirty. Mixed night.
Eight filter coffees for a festival-eve meeting - two lids off in transit, one cup half empty on arrival. Pack them better.
Nice festival vibes but the room was so packed we nursed one hot chocolate between two at a wobbly two-seater. Meh evening.
Match crowd mein takeaway snack ke liye eighteen minute lage - quantity theek thi but intezar zyada. Off-peak aana better.
Kids wanted the post-match waffle; it took thirty-five minutes with three reminders. Kind staff, just drowned in orders tonight.
Festival ke shor ne kaam impossible kar diya, table bhi do baar bump hui crowd se, aur refills slow ho gaye. Not a work night.
Match-night order placed at six, arrived at eight-thirty, sandwich stone cold. The game was over; so was my patience.
Festival delivery disaster - latte cup tipped over, croissant drowned in the spill. Salvaged half a pastry. Never again on event nights.
Post-match family dinner: fifty-minute wait, cranky kids, and the waffle finally arrived undercooked in the middle. Should have cooked at home.
Match ke baad itni bheed ki counter tak pahunchna mushkil tha. Order diya, pachaas minute baad bhi nahi aaya. Chale gaye.
Match-eve counter meltdown - eighteen minutes for one coffee, ticket lost once in the chaos. Good shot wasted on a broken queue.
Ordered cheese toast and an iced latte for the match - the toast came cold and the drink hot instead of iced. Wrong on both counts.
Festival crowd turned the cafe into a stadium concourse - no plugs, deafening chatter, twenty minutes for a drink. Work was impossible.
Match night and regulars get no love - twenty-five minutes for a flat white while delivery tickets kept jumping ahead. Hurt, honestly.
Pre-ordered for a match screening - pickup took thirty minutes, two sandwiches missing, cold brews gone warm. Screening started dry.
Festival crowd and nobody at the counter acknowledged me for ten minutes. The chai, when it came, was lovely - which stings more.
Match-surge delivery: bag arrived crushed, cold brew cup dented, fries limp and sad. Eighty minutes for a soggy dinner.
Kids' dinner ordered at seven, arrived nine-thirty - pasta cold, shake missing entirely. Two hungry kids and a ruined evening.
Jeet celebrate karna tha, bana forty minute ka wait cheese toast ke liye shoulder-to-shoulder crowd mein. Ghar jaana better tha.
Festival date gone wrong - forty minutes for a rose latte and nobody checked on us even once. The drink was pretty; the night was not.
Twenty minutes for a takeaway filter coffee on match eve, then the lid was not pressed on - leaked all over my notes. Double fail.
A 230-rupee hot chocolate arrived cold with the marshmallows melted into glue. Match-night surge is no excuse for this.
Match-final order: waffle box crushed flat, syrup everywhere except on the waffle, everything cold. Straight into the bin.
Thirty minutes for a takeaway espresso on match night, ticket lost twice, cashier just shrugged. Worst coffee run of my life.
After the match we waited an hour, got seated, waited thirty more, then told the kitchen was closed to new orders. With hungry kids. Unforgivable.
Festival-night order arrived with completely wrong items - nothing we ordered, a drink spilled in the bag, everything cold. Total write-off.
Match night pe aaye - bheed mein dhakke khaye, staff ne ignore kiya, order hi nahi liya gaya. Ghar chale gaye bhookhe.
Match-eve chaos mein pachchees minute lage cappuccino ke liye, aur mila ek milky latte. This counter has lost me.
Ninety-minute match-night delivery: fries like cold leather, cheese toast rubbery, bag soaked through at the bottom. Festival of failures.
Stood invisible at the counter for twenty minutes on festival night while others were served around me. Left without ordering. Embarrassing.
Client match-screening order: eighteen cappuccinos, delivered ninety minutes late, seven missing, rest cold. Never trusting them for events.
Waited forever in the festival crush, and the cheesecake sold out while we stood in line. Nobody even apologised. Chaos won tonight.
Match night made it a standing-room shouting match. Cold brew took twenty-five minutes, no seats, no hope of working. Never again.
Fries manga tha, bees minute baad cheese toast diya aur bola 'same hai'. Match crowd mein poori service toot gayi. Bakwaas.
Sheltered from festival crowds, ordered, waited thirty minutes while delivery slips flew past me. Left into the noise, empty-handed.
Ordered a sandwich for the match - arrived after the final over, cold and the wrong filling. Both the delivery and my evening, ruined.
